\section{Data Specifications}

The empirical specifications vary along two dimensions: the
inflation--expectation pair and the measure of the Phillips-curve forcing
variable. Table~\ref{tab:data_specs} summarizes the alternatives considered
throughout the estimation.

\begin{table}[H]
\centering
\caption{Empirical Data Specifications}
\label{tab:data_specs}
\small
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.3}

% --------------------------------------------------
% Panel A
% --------------------------------------------------
\begin{tabular}{@{}p{0.28\textwidth}p{0.55\textwidth}@{}}
\toprule
\multicolumn{2}{@{}l}{\textbf{Panel A. Inflation--Expectation Pairs}} \\
\textbf{Inflation Measure} & \textbf{Expected Inflation Measure} \\
\midrule
PPI
& GDP price index inflation forecast \\

Headline CPI
& CPI inflation forecast \\

Core CPI
& CPI inflation forecast \\
\end{tabular}

\vspace{1.5em}

% --------------------------------------------------
% Panel B
% --------------------------------------------------
\begin{tabular}{@{}p{0.28\textwidth}p{0.55\textwidth}@{}}
\toprule
\multicolumn{2}{@{}l}{\textbf{Panel B. Phillips-Curve Forcing Variables}} \\
\textbf{Measure} & \textbf{Interpretation} \\
\midrule
Inverse markup
& Proxy for real marginal cost \\

Negative unemployment gap
& Labor-market slack measure \\

Beveridge--Nelson output gap
& Output-gap measure based on the Beveridge--Nelson decomposition \\

Hodrick--Prescott output gap
& Output-gap measure based on the Hodrick--Prescott filter \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\end{table}

Each inflation--expectation pair is combined with the alternative forcing-variable
measures in the model specifications below. This structure allows the estimated
Phillips-curve relationship to be compared across both inflation measurement
and the empirical proxy used for economic slack or real marginal cost.
